plain_description.what: No calls. A regression was refitted on existing verdict caches for the same matches: pairwise and pointwise (single-answer grading) formats, two judge families (grok, Mistral), and a version with no reference answer in the prompt as a control.
plain_description.why: It asks why the judge follows the reference answer more than actual correctness: is it the format, the judge model, or the recipe?
plain_description.information: It separates 'the judge copies the reference' from 'the judge reasons for itself', and shows whether the result depends on the judge model. Result: done, descriptive. The control failed, so the earlier 2.7:1 'reference beats correctness' ratio is an upper bound. In the grading format, showing a reference made the judge lean on it more and on its own assessment less. A follow-up found this displacement does not happen in the pairwise format. grok and Mistral behaved almost identically, so it is the recipe, not the model. Note: older question pool, ruled 'history, not evidence'.
